$comment: FOUNDATION loop permissions. Committed and reviewable — changing what an
unattended session may do is a DIFF, not a keystroke.
ALLOW is scoped to what the RELAY queue actually needs: git/gh, the node
toolchain, the repo's own scripts, docker compose + exec (the QA stack and
read-only prod queries), and reads. It is broad within the repo and narrow
DENY is the important half, and it is not a duplicate of the guardrails —
it is the mechanical backstop UNDER them. Each entry is something the
canon already forbids in words; these make the words unable to fail:
· force-push and history rewrite  — the 2026-07-27/28 purges
· deleting a pre-* rollback tag   — sacred by canon
· docker compose down / stop      — the prod stack, and co-tenants
· raw prisma migrate against prod — deploy-prod.sh is the only path
· nginx / systemctl on the host   — co-tenants share this ingress
· stripe live keys                — TEST MODE ONLY
⚠️ DENY BEATS ALLOW. A pattern here overrides any allow entry above, so a
broad allow cannot accidentally re-open one of these.
